stories.title: Attackers Exploit Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days That May Form an Attack Chain
stories.abstract: CISA added nine vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including critical flaws in Sangoma Switchvox, SonicWall SMA1000 appliances, and several open-source tools. These bugs, ranging from SQL injection to command execution, are currently being leveraged by attackers in active campaigns.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild, posing a high risk of unauthorized access or remote code execution on critical infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches for Sangoma Switchvox, SonicWall SMA1000, and affected open-source software immediately.

stories.title: Google Releases Chrome Update to Patch Actively Exploited V8 Zero-Day
stories.abstract: Google has patched twelve vulnerabilities in Chrome, including a high-severity type confusion flaw in the V8 engine, identified as CVE-2026-85046. The company confirmed that this specific vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild.
stories.why: Active exploitation of browser engine vulnerabilities poses a significant risk for remote code execution and system compromise.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 152.0.7977.82 or later.

stories.title: CISA Adds Seven Exploited Flaws as Attackers Deploy Reverse Shells and Crypto Miners
stories.abstract: CISA has added seven vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including two critical flaws in SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances. Attackers are actively leveraging these bugs to deploy reverse shells and cryptocurrency miners on compromised systems.
stories.why: Active exploitation of critical-severity vulnerabilities in edge network appliances poses a significant risk of unauthorized remote access and persistent infrastructure compromise.
stories.action: Update SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances to the latest patched firmware versions immediately.

stories.title: Google warns of new Chrome zero-day flaw exploited in attacks
stories.abstract: Google released a security update for Chrome addressing twelve vulnerabilities, including a high-severity type confusion flaw in the V8 engine. This specific zero-day vulnerability is currently being exploited in the wild, marking the sixth such incident for the browser this year.
stories.why: Active exploitation of V8 engine vulnerabilities allows attackers to bypass browser security boundaries, potentially leading to remote code execution on user systems.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 152 or later immediately.

stories.title: Researcher Releases FalconFlank PoC Showing Privilege Escalation in CrowdStrike Falcon
stories.abstract: A security researcher released a proof-of-concept exploit dubbed FalconFlank, which leverages a flaw in CrowdStrike Falcon's remediation of malicious macros. The vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges to SYSTEM level on fully patched Windows systems.
stories.why: Privilege escalation vulnerabilities in endpoint protection software provide attackers with a direct path to full system compromise and persistence.

stories.title: JFrog security advisory (AV26-867) – Update 1
PostgreSQL Fixes 12-Year-Old Logical Decoding Flaw Enabling Replication-Role Code Execution
stories.abstract: PostgreSQL patched a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-6471, present since 2014. The flaw allows users with replication privileges to execute arbitrary code as the database service account, potentially leading to full server compromise and persistent backdoors.
stories.why: Replication roles are often granted to automated tools, making this a significant escalation vector for attackers who compromise those service accounts.
stories.action: Update PostgreSQL to versions 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, 14.24, or later.

stories.title: G7 urges organizations to prepare for quantum cyber threats
stories.abstract: The G7 and CISA have issued a joint advisory urging organizations to begin transitioning to post-quantum cryptography. The guidance emphasizes the necessity of preparing for future quantum computing capabilities that could potentially compromise current encryption standards and sensitive data security.
stories.why: Quantum advancements threaten current asymmetric encryption, necessitating long-term planning for cryptographic agility to protect data with long-term confidentiality requirements.

stories.title: Critical Elementor Pro flaw exploited to take over WordPress sites
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in the Elementor Pro WordPress plugin to inject webshells. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to execute arbitrary commands on affected servers, potentially leading to full site compromise.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in widely used plugins provide an easy entry point for persistent backdoors and server-side attacks.
stories.action: Update Elementor Pro to the latest patched version immediately.

stories.title: Critical Citrix NetScaler auth bypass now leveraged in attacks
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler, identified as CVE-2026-19490. Security researchers have confirmed that the flaw is currently being leveraged in real-world attacks to compromise vulnerable infrastructure.
stories.why: Unauthenticated attackers can potentially gain unauthorized access to sensitive NetScaler environments, leading to full system compromise or data exfiltration.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches from Citrix immediately.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation 1756-ENBT Module
stories.abstract: Rockwell Automation has disclosed multiple vulnerabilities across several products, including the 1756-ENBT module, ArmorStart LT, CompactLogix/ControlLogix controllers, and FactoryTalk Historian ME. These flaws range from denial-of-service conditions to potential remote code execution via out-of-bounds write and buffer overflow issues.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical infrastructure sectors, potentially allowing attackers to crash industrial control systems or execute arbitrary code on affected hardware.
stories.action: Review Rockwell Automation security advisories and apply available firmware or software updates immediately.

stories.title: Prolific Microsoft 0-day hunter drops CrowdStrike Falcon exploit PoC
stories.abstract: A security researcher has released a proof-of-concept exploit targeting CrowdStrike Falcon. The disclosure highlights potential vulnerabilities within the endpoint protection platform's architecture, specifically concerning how the software interacts with the underlying operating system.
stories.why: Exploits targeting security agents can be weaponized to bypass endpoint detection or gain elevated system privileges.

stories.title: Over 440,000 Exploit Attempts Target Super Forms and Elementor Pro RCE Flaws
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively targeting critical remote code execution vulnerabilities within the Super Forms and Elementor Pro WordPress plugins. Wordfence reports over 440,000 exploitation attempts, primarily leveraging a file upload flaw in Super Forms that permits unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary code.
stories.why: These plugins are widely deployed, and the vulnerabilities allow full site compromise by unauthenticated remote actors.
stories.action: Update Super Forms and Elementor Pro to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: HPE Patches Critical RCE Vulnerabilities in AOS-CX
stories.abstract: HPE released security updates for its AOS-CX network operating system to resolve nearly two dozen vulnerabilities. The most severe of these flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-73749, is a critical remote code execution vulnerability carrying a maximum CVSS score of 9.8.
stories.why: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in network infrastructure allow attackers to gain full administrative control over switches, facilitating lateral movement and network-wide compromise.
stories.action: Update AOS-CX firmware to the latest version provided by HPE.

stories.title: don't plan a con with these guys #defcon #technews #hacker
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified a critical two-click remote code execution vulnerability in the Omaki Linux distribution. The flaw resides in the OS's Chromium extension, allowing attackers to leverage malicious configuration files during video downloads to achieve arbitrary command execution.
stories.why: The vulnerability highlights supply chain risks in niche, viral Linux distributions that bundle custom configurations and third-party extensions without rigorous security auditing.
stories.action: Update Omaki Linux and its Chromium extension to the latest available versions immediately.

stories.title: In Other News: Microsoft’s Cloud Patches, Hacked Dropbox Accounts, Guardio’s $1.1B Valuation
stories.abstract: Microsoft released security updates for its cloud infrastructure, while unauthorized actors successfully breached approximately 5,000 Dropbox user accounts. Additionally, the browser security firm Guardio has reached a valuation of $1.1 billion following its latest funding round.
stories.why: Cloud service patches indicate active vulnerability remediation, and the Dropbox incident highlights ongoing risks to user account credentials.

stories.title: Tycon Systems TPDIN-Monitor-WEB2 (Update A)
stories.abstract: Multiple critical vulnerabilities affect Tycon Systems TPDIN-Monitor-WEB2 and WEB3 devices. Flaws include missing authentication, hard-coded credentials, and cleartext storage of sensitive data, potentially allowing attackers to manipulate physical equipment, reset devices, or intercept traffic.
stories.why: These devices control industrial infrastructure; exploitation could lead to physical damage, unauthorized access to sensitive credentials, or complete system compromise.
stories.action: Update TPDIN-Monitor-WEB2 to version 2.4.5 or later and check vendor guidance for WEB3 patches.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation ArmorStart LT
stories.abstract: Rockwell Automation ArmorStart LT versions 2.001 and earlier are vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting and resource exhaustion flaws. These issues could allow unauthorized script execution within a user's browser or lead to a complete denial of service for the device's web interface.
stories.why: Exploitation allows attackers to compromise administrative sessions or disrupt critical industrial control operations by crashing the web server.

stories.title: Rockwell Automation ControlFLASH
Inductive Automation Ignition
stories.abstract: Inductive Automation Ignition versions 8.1.53 and older contain a vulnerability where default permission settings allow any authenticated user to create projects. This flaw stems from an insecure configuration that permits unauthorized project creation through gateway scripts.
stories.why: Unauthorized project creation in industrial control software can lead to arbitrary code execution and full system compromise within critical infrastructure environments.
stories.action: Update Inductive Automation Ignition to version 8.1.54 or later.

stories.title: OPCFoundation OPC UA LocalDiscoveryServer (LDS)
stories.abstract: A privilege escalation vulnerability in OPCFoundation OPC UA LocalDiscoveryServer installers prior to version 1.04.420 allows attackers to intercept high-privilege terminal windows during the installation process, potentially enabling the execution of arbitrary commands with elevated system rights.
stories.why: This flaw poses a significant risk to critical infrastructure environments where unauthorized command execution could lead to full system compromise.
stories.action: Update OPC UA LocalDiscoveryServer to version 1.04.420 or later.

stories.title: IXON VPN Client
SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days Enable Unauthenticated RCE
Thomson Reuters Court Software Breach May Have Exposed SSNs and Sealed Data
stories.abstract: Thomson Reuters reported a data breach involving its C-Track court management platform. Unauthorized access to files occurred in March 2026, potentially compromising sensitive records, including Social Security numbers, across multiple U.S. states, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Ontario, Canada.
stories.why: The exposure of sensitive judicial records and PII poses significant risks for identity theft and the compromise of sealed legal proceedings.

stories.title: Critical Cisco Nexus 9000 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Remote Attackers Run Code as Root
stories.abstract: Cisco patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-20212, in specific Nexus 9000 switches. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to gain root access. Additionally, Cisco released IOS XR updates addressing seven vulnerabilities, including two critical issues lacking available workarounds.
stories.why: Remote root access on core network infrastructure poses a severe risk of total system compromise and lateral movement within the enterprise environment.
stories.action: Update affected Nexus 9000 switches and IOS XR devices to the latest patched firmware versions.

stories.title: [Control Systems] Siemens security advisory (AV26-881)
stories.abstract: Siemens and Schneider Electric have released security advisories addressing vulnerabilities in Mendix SAML modules, NetBotz monitoring hardware, and PowerChute Serial Shutdown software. These flaws include risks of account hijacking and improper authentication controls across various industrial and enterprise management systems.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in industrial control and management software can provide attackers with unauthorized access or control over critical infrastructure and enterprise environments.
stories.action: Update Mendix SAML, NetBotz, and PowerChute software to the latest versions specified in the vendor advisories.

stories.title: Your Employee’s Password Appeared in an Infostealer Log. Now What?
Pyramid Solutions NetStaX EtherNet/IP Stack
stories.abstract: A critical stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Pyramid Solutions NetStaX EtherNet/IP stack allows remote attackers to trigger memory corruption or device crashes. The flaw affects various adapter and scanner development kits, potentially enabling unauthorized remote code execution without triggering standard error logs.
stories.why: This vulnerability poses a severe risk to industrial control systems, potentially allowing attackers to compromise critical infrastructure components remotely.
stories.action: Contact Pyramid Solutions to obtain and apply the necessary patches for your specific NetStaX development kit.

stories.title: SUSE Linux security advisory (AV26-882)
stories.abstract: SUSE has released a security update for Rancher versions prior to 2.15.1 to address identified vulnerabilities. Administrators should review the official advisory and apply the latest patches to ensure their container management environments remain secure.
stories.why: Unpatched container management platforms are high-value targets for privilege escalation and unauthorized cluster access.
stories.action: Update Rancher to version 2.15.1 or later.

stories.title: 39 New Methods That Compromise Passkey Authentication
stories.abstract: Security researchers identified 39 distinct attack vectors targeting passkey implementations. These methods exploit weaknesses in enrollment, recovery flows, and authentication prompts rather than attempting to break the underlying FIDO2 cryptographic standards, highlighting vulnerabilities in how services integrate and manage these credentials.
stories.why: It demonstrates that passkeys are not a silver bullet and remain susceptible to implementation flaws and social engineering within the authentication lifecycle.

stories.title: BraZetsu Malware Turns Compromised Windows Hosts Into Criminal Marketplace Inventory
stories.abstract: A new Python-based malware framework named BraZetsu is being used by initial access brokers to transform infected Windows machines into commodities. The toolkit automates the management and sale of compromised host access, streamlining the commercialization of illicit network entry points.
stories.why: It signals a shift toward specialized, automated infrastructure for initial access brokers, increasing the efficiency of ransomware and data theft operations.

stories.title: OpenAI Pledges $1 Billion to Bring Frontier AI to Critical Infrastructure Defenders
Schneider Electric Easergy, EcoStruxture, PowerLogic, and Saitel Products (Update A)
stories.abstract: Schneider Electric has identified vulnerabilities affecting several Easergy and EcoStruxure power automation products. These components, used in critical electrical distribution and substation management, are currently under review for security flaws that could impact operational infrastructure.
stories.why: Vulnerabilities in industrial control systems and power grid hardware pose significant risks to operational technology availability and physical infrastructure safety.
stories.action: Review the official Schneider Electric security advisory for specific firmware update requirements.

stories.title: ISC Stormcast For Friday, September 4th, 2026 https://isc.sans.edu/podcastdetail/10082, (Fri, Sep 4th)
stories.abstract: The SANS Internet Storm Center has released its daily security briefing podcast for September 4, 2026, covering current threat intelligence and operational security updates for the cybersecurity community.
stories.why: Provides timely situational awareness regarding emerging vulnerabilities and active exploitation trends observed by the SANS ISC global sensor network.

stories.title: AMD security advisory (AV26-879)
stories.abstract: AMD has released a security advisory detailing firmware vulnerabilities across multiple EPYC, Athlon, and Instinct processor lines. Users must update their system BIOS or platform initialization firmware to the specified minimum versions to mitigate these hardware-level security risks.
stories.why: Unpatched processor firmware can expose systems to privilege escalation, data leakage, or side-channel attacks that bypass traditional OS-level security controls.
stories.action: Update system BIOS/UEFI to the minimum versions specified in AMD advisory AV26-879.

stories.title: Pegasus Zero-Click Spyware Exploit Infects Serbian Student Movement Member's iPhone
stories.abstract: Citizen Lab and the SHARE Foundation identified a zero-click iMessage exploit used to deploy NSO Group's Pegasus spyware against a Serbian student activist. The infection occurred without any user interaction, highlighting the ongoing risk of sophisticated surveillance tools targeting political dissidents.
stories.why: It demonstrates the continued efficacy of zero-click mobile exploits against high-risk individuals, bypassing standard user-based security defenses.

stories.title: F5 security advisory (AV26-878)
stories.abstract: F5 has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across its product suite, including BIG-IP, BIG-IQ, and various NGINX components. Administrators should review the advisory to identify affected versions and plan necessary maintenance to secure their infrastructure.
stories.why: Unpatched vulnerabilities in core networking and load-balancing infrastructure provide high-value targets for attackers seeking network persistence or traffic interception.
stories.action: Update BIG-IP, BIG-IQ, and NGINX components to the latest patched versions listed in advisory K000162872.

stories.title: Jenkins security advisory (AV26-877)
stories.abstract: The Jenkins project released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across its core platform and several widely used plugins, including those for GitLab, Microsoft Entra ID, LDAP, and SAML integration. Users should verify their current versions against the latest patched releases.
stories.why: Unpatched Jenkins instances are frequent targets for initial access, remote code execution, and credential harvesting within CI/CD pipelines.
stories.action: Update Jenkins core and all listed plugins to the latest available versions immediately.

stories.title: Cisco security advisory (AV26-876)
stories.abstract: Cisco has released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across its product line, including remote code execution risks in Nexus 9000 switches, denial of service flaws in various IP and video phones, and security hardening requirements for IOS XR software.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities expose critical network infrastructure and communication endpoints to potential remote exploitation and service disruption.
stories.action: Review Cisco security advisories and apply patches for affected IOS XR, Nexus, and IP phone firmware.

stories.title: PaperCut security advisory (AV26-858) – Update 2
stories.abstract: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. These flaws affect PaperCut MF and NG print management software, and active exploitation has been confirmed in the wild.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are actively being exploited, posing a significant risk of unauthorized access or system compromise for organizations running PaperCut software.
stories.action: Update PaperCut MF and NG to the latest emergency patch releases immediately.

stories.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
stories.abstract: The FBI is investigating a dark web service offering over 153 million driver's license scans from the U.S. and Canada. The data appears to originate from a breach at a Louisiana-based identity verification firm, facilitating widespread identity theft.
stories.why: This massive exposure of government-issued identification documents significantly lowers the barrier for sophisticated account takeover and synthetic identity fraud.

stories.title: New Ted Backdoor Hides Inside Victims' Own HAProxy Builds to Intercept Web Traffic
stories.abstract: Attackers compromised two South Korean organizations by replacing their HAProxy load balancer binaries with trojanized versions. The malicious implant, dubbed Ted, intercepts web traffic and serves modified content to specific targets, requiring prior host-level code execution to deploy.
stories.why: This highlights a sophisticated supply chain compromise where attackers manipulate core infrastructure binaries to maintain stealthy, persistent access to network traffic.
stories.action: Audit HAProxy binary integrity and verify build provenance on critical load-balancing infrastructure.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Langflow and Rails Flaws in Credential-Probing and C2 Activity
Coder's registry infrastructure compromised to push malicious modules
stories.abstract: Threat actors breached Coder's Cloudflare configuration to inject rogue registry servers. These servers distributed compromised Terraform modules designed to exfiltrate sensitive credentials from developer environments.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting infrastructure-as-code tools allow attackers to harvest secrets directly from developer workstations and CI/CD pipelines.
stories.action: Audit Terraform module sources and rotate any credentials exposed in environments where these modules were recently deployed.

stories.title: US, Britain to coordinate on scam center takedowns
Phishing Campaign Sends Millions of Emails Using Invisible Unicode to Evade Filters
Companies Have Six Months to Prepare for Automated Attacks
Exchange Online outage causes email delays, 'Server busy' errors
Security Vulnerability in a Voting System
stories.abstract: Researchers demonstrated that AI tools can deanonymize voter records by correlating public cast-vote records with early-voting lists. This technique reconstructs the sequence of ballots cast, effectively linking individual voters to their specific selections without requiring direct access to voting hardware or private networks.
stories.why: It highlights a significant privacy failure in election infrastructure where public data, when processed by AI, compromises ballot secrecy.

stories.title: AI Is Ending the Era of Hidden Vulnerabilities — Are Vendors Ready?
Extradited Russian Hacker Faces Charges Over Excel Malware Campaign That Infected Thousands
Plex Urges Immediate Updates After Patching Multiple Undisclosed Security Flaws
Another Artifactory CVE under attack by AI agents or humans
GPT-6 Astra Scores 100% on ExploitBench as OpenAI Blocks PoC Exploit Requests
Researchers Use Claude to Port Pre-Auth RCE Exploit From One PLC Model to Another
Microsoft says some users can’t open the Teams desktop client
Communicating Under Pressure: Best Practices for Service Providers
US military disabled ad tracking on troops’ devices following reports of targeted attacks
